newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Iranian president arrives in Tanzania.
newsitem.headline: Iranian president arrives in Tanzania.

text.p: Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani arrived in Tanzania on Monday on the fourth leg of a six-nation African tour to improve ties and drum up business.
Rafsanjani arrived in Dar es Salaam from Khartoum where following his mediation Islamist Sudan and neighbouring Uganda agreed to resume diplomatic relations broken in April last year.
Rafsanjani was welcomed by Tanzanian President Benjamin Mkapa and Iranian women chanting "Allahu Akbar" (God is Greatest) before driving into the Indian Ocean capital for talks.

The presidential motorcade was slightly delayed by a dispute between one of Rafsanjani's bodyguards and a Tanzanian military officer over seating and an argument between other Tanzanian and Iranian escorts.
The route into the city centre was lined by an estimated 20,000 people including many members of the Moslem community, which makes up some 30 percent of Tanzania's population.
Officials said bilateral and trade issues would top the agenda for talks and Rafsanjani would visit Iranian-funded aid projects including schools on Zanzibar island, which is 97 percent Moslem.
Rafsanjani arrived in Dar es Salaam from Khartoum after visiting Uganda and starting his African tour in Kenya. He is scheduled to visit South Africa and Zimbabwe after Tanzania.
Diplomats said the tour was designed to reduce Iran's international isolation and the impact of U.S. sanctions. Washington accuses Iran of sponsoring terrorism, a charge Iran denies.
Rafsanjani has said Iran is offering the hand of brotherhood to Africa after its land was raped by Western colonialists.

The tour comes a month after U.S. President Bill Clinton tightened sanctions against Iran. The law penalises non-U.S. firms that invest $40 million or more a year in the oil and gas sectors of Iran or Libya.
Iran has steadily stepped up its diplomatic presence in Africa and tried to boost cultural and religious links with Moslems on the world's poorest continent.
